license.value: Apache-2.0 in card metadata (license: apache-2.0, license_link: LICENSE), but the repo has NO LICENSE file (raw/main/LICENSE returns 404; not in siblings). params.value: 19,432,294,256 BF16 params (HF safetensors count, includes the vision tower; MTP is in separate files in the quant repos). Card: about 19B total, about 3B active, plus a 0.4B MTP layer. Pruned from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: config.json is identical to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B except num_experts 128 vs 256 (plus pad_token_id, router_aux_loss_coef 0.0, use_cache), so the routed experts per layer were cut in half. Vendor reply in the GGUF discussion #2 (2026-11-02): 'the model was pruned from the base model, though the pruning method was not REAP'. The method is not disclosed. Active estimate from config: about 1.13B expert params (8 routed + 1 shared x 3 x 2048 x 512 x 40 layers) + about 1.8B attention/GDN + 0.51B lm_head = about 3.4B read per token.

architecture.value: Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration (model_type qwen3_5_moe), the same as Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. 40 layers, full_attention_interval 4: 10 full-attention layers (16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head_dim 256, output gate, partial rotary 0.25, rope_theta 1e7, mrope) and 30 Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers (16 key heads x 128, 32 value heads x 128, conv kernel 4, SSM state float32). Hidden 2048. MoE: 128 routed experts (moe_intermediate 512) + 1 shared expert (512), 8 routed per token. Vocab 248,320, untied embeddings. 1 MTP layer. Vision tower: 27 layers, hidden 1152.

context_length.value: max_position_embeddings 262,144 (tokenizer model_max_length 262144); card says YaRN factor 4 reaches about 1M. The card recommends keeping at least 128K to preserve thinking quality. On this GPU: about 128k (llama.cpp Q4_K_M, f16 KV) or 256k (q8_0 KV); vLLM NVFP4 about 128k BF16 KV / 257k FP8 KV with --language-model-only.

modalities.value: Image and video input + text output (pipeline_tag image-text-to-text; card says 'natively multimodal'). Text-only path: vLLM --language-model-only (skips the BF16 vision tower, about 0.84 GiB); llama.cpp: do not load the mmproj (pass --no-mmproj with -hf, because -hf would otherwise auto-fetch mmproj-Groot-19B-A3B-261023-BF16.gguf, 0.84 GiB).

thinking.how_to_toggle:
Thinking is on by default: the template appends '<think>
' to the generation prompt, and enable_thinking=false appends an empty '<think>

</think>

'. The card says there are no /think or /nothink soft switches. vLLM: per request extra_body chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false}; server default --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' (flag present in vllm/entrypoints/common/cli_args.py at v0.33.0); --reasoning-parser qwen3 puts the trace in 'reasoning' (the card says reasoning_content; the baseline says vLLM v0.33.0 uses 'reasoning'). llama.cpp b12407: --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' or --reasoning off as the server default, with per-request chat_template_kwargs in the body; --reasoning-budget N. Ollama: 'think' request field only if the model's capabilities include thinking; the only Ollama upload shows only the vision capability, so the toggle is unverified there. TEMPLATE DISCREPANCY: chat_template.jinja (used by the official GGUF, template length 7536) re-emits <think>reasoning</think> for EVERY past assistant turn and ignores preserve_thinking, while the template embedded in tokenizer_config.json (7764 chars, used by bartowski's GGUF) drops past reasoning unless preserve_thinking=true, as the card describes. vLLM/transformers 5.x normally prefer chat_template.jinja (inferred).

vllm.arch_supported: Yes. v0.33.0 registry.py line 205 Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM, lines 618-620 Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration, line 740 Qwen3_5MoeMTP (MTP). Card asks for vLLM >= 0.19.1.
vllm.kv_math: Budget 16303 MiB x 0.92 = 14999 MiB = 14.65 GiB. NVFP4 shards 11.78 GiB (vision tower included, BF16, estimated 0.84 GiB from the mmproj size). KV per token = 2 x 10 full-attn layers x 2 KV heads x 256 x 2 B = 20,480 B BF16, 10,240 B FP8. GDN state per sequence = 30 x (32x128x128x4 B SSM + 8192x3x2 B conv) = 0.06 GiB. (a) With vision: 14.65 - 11.78 - 1.2 = 1.67 GiB, minus 0.06 = 1.61 GiB -> 84.5k tokens BF16 / 169k FP8. (b) --language-model-only: 14.65 - 10.94 - 1.2 = 2.51, minus 0.06 = 2.45 GiB -> 128.5k BF16 / 257k FP8 (cap 262,144). (c) LM-only + MTP (0.82 GiB): 1.63 GiB -> 85k BF16 / 171k FP8. The checkpoint ships an FP8 kv_cache_scheme; FP8 KV on sm_120 needs --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN (baseline, FlashInfer race #61239).
vllm.quant_on_sm120: Experts are NVFP4 weight-only (input_activations null), so compressed_tensors_moe.py at v0.33.0 builds CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod(use_a16=True). oracle/nvfp4.py walks FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, CUTEDSL, CUTLASS, VLLM_CUTLASS, MARLIN; prioritize_humming only moves Humming ahead on cc 90 (humming/priority.py), so on sm_120 the MoE uses MARLIN W4A16 (inferred from the selection order; it matches the kernels logged in #54331). This avoids the W4A4 FlashInfer CUTLASS JIT host-RAM spike (#46268). Attention/GDN projections are FP8 W8A8 static per-tensor (CUTLASS FP8, supported on sm_120).
vllm.tool_call_parser: qwen3_coder (or qwen3_xml, same class at v0.33.0)
vllm.min_version: 0.19.1 per the card; Qwen3_5Moe and the parsers are present at v0.33.0
vllm.serve_command: docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --memory 24g -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 -v $HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0 GrootTeam/Groot-19B-A3B-261023-NVFP4 --served-model-name groot-19b-a3b --language-model-only --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --max-num-seqs 2 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
vllm.known_issues: #54331 (OPEN): sm_120 hybrid-GDN NVFP4 (qwen3_5_moe, MARLIN NvFp4 MoE backend, also nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4) dies under sustained high-concurrency load whenever CUDA graphs are on, still reported on 0.26-0.28; only enforce_eager survived. That is the same arch and kernel path as this checkpoint, so add --enforce-eager if it crashes. Hybrid prefix caching uses mamba_cache_mode align. MTP speculative decoding costs 0.82 GiB and cuts the KV pool to about 85k BF16. The card's serve commands use the wrong repo id 'Groot/...'.

llamacpp.arch_supported: Yes. b12407 src/llama-arch.cpp line 46 { LLM_ARCH_QWEN35MOE, "qwen35moe" }; the HF GGUF metadata of the official and bartowski files says architecture qwen35moe, context_length 262144.
llamacpp.quant: Q4_K_M (official, 10.86 GiB; mradermacher i1-Q4_K_M is the same size with imatrix; bartowski Q4_K_M is 11.63 GiB)
llamacpp.offload_plan: All layers on GPU, no --n-cpu-moe. VRAM: 10.86 GiB weights + KV f16 at 131072 = 131072 x 20,480 B = 2.50 GiB + recurrent state about 0.06 GiB + compute buffers about 1 GiB (248k vocab) = about 14.4 GiB of 15.9 GiB. 262144 with q8_0 KV (about 10,880 B/token) = 2.66 GiB -> about 14.6 GiB, tight but fits; 262144 f16 (5.0 GiB) does not fit. Context checkpoints for the hybrid model live in host RAM. The card's own estimate: 128K on a 16 GB card.
llamacpp.tool_calling_note: The template uses the Qwen3-Coder XML format that llama.cpp's --jinja chat parser handles for Qwen3.5/3.6. Because the arch and template family match Qwen3.6, the open issues #30357 (reasoning/whitespace not round-trippable, prefix-cache invalidation, full re-prefill) and #30118 (tool call leaking into content) likely apply (inferred, untested on Groot). The official GGUF embeds the always-preserve-thinking chat_template.jinja; bartowski embeds the tokenizer_config variant. OpenCode reasoningField 'reasoning_content' for llama.cpp.

speed_notes: Inferred bound for llama.cpp Q4_K_M on this GPU: about 3.4B params read per token x about 0.61 B/param (11.66e9 B / 18.99e9 GGUF params) = about 2.1 GB/token; 896 GB/s / 2.1 GB = about 430 tok/s ceiling, so about 150-250 tok/s decode at short context realistically (inferred; baseline anchor: desktop RTX 5080 gpt-oss-20b about 205 tok/s). Everything stays in VRAM, so it should be much faster than Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with --n-cpu-moe 21. Third-party measured on RTX PRO 6000 (1792 GB/s), vLLM NVFP4+MTP: decode 379 tok/s single stream, 303 tok/s at 120k context, prefill 27k tok/s at 32k (Blackwall). One user reported half the speed of Qwen3.6-35B Q4_K_M with the same settings (GGUF discussion #3, unexplained). Not measured on this machine.

opencode_fit.recommended_runtime: llama.cpp (server-cuda-b12407) with the official Q4_K_M, all on GPU; vLLM NVFP4 as second
opencode_fit.recommended_context: 131072 with f16 KV (about 14.4 GiB VRAM); 65536-131072 on vLLM NVFP4 --language-model-only with FP8 KV
opencode_fit.caveats: A strong candidate to replace Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (#1) on this 16 GB laptop, because it fits fully in VRAM at 128k with Qwen3.6-class tool calling and parsers. Do not promote it until it is measured here: (1) anonymous publisher (user account, unverified org, team question unanswered), no LICENSE file, undisclosed pruning method and data; (2) every agentic score is self-reported, and on the vendor's own chart it LOSES to Qwen3.6 on SWE-bench Verified (31.66 vs 36.27) and ties on BFCL v4; the only third-party eval (Blackwall) is a single run without a Qwen3.6 comparison; (3) community reports of knowledge loss and alleged ideological data shaping (GGUF discussion #3), only English and Chinese output, and altered verbatim text in file paths (discussion #5), which matters for a coding agent; (4) chat_template.jinja differs from the tokenizer_config template (always preserves past thinking), and llama.cpp issues #30357/#30118 for this arch likely apply; (5) vLLM NVFP4 path shares #54331 (hybrid GDN + Marlin NVFP4 crash under load with CUDA graphs on sm_120). Run an A/B against Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with the same OpenCode tasks, thinking on and off.

gaps: Publisher identity and pruning method are undisclosed (vendor says only 'not REAP'); no paper, blog or LICENSE file.
No independent agentic-coding eval (SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench) by a neutral party; Blackwall is a single third-party run with its own suite and no Qwen3.6 baseline.
Vision tower size inside the NVFP4 shards is estimated from the 0.84 GiB mmproj, not counted per tensor.
Which chat template vLLM v0.33.0 actually applies (chat_template.jinja vs tokenizer_config) was not confirmed by running it.
Whether vLLM uses the checkpoint's FP8 kv_cache_scheme scales under --kv-cache-dtype auto was not checked.
Ollama loading of the HF qwen35moe GGUF and its tool/thinking support are unverified.
llama.cpp compute-buffer size for the 248k vocab is estimated (about 1 GiB), not measured; no tok/s measured on this laptop.
Whether llama.cpp #30357 and #30118 reproduce on Groot is untested.
